role: CRE lender and debt underwriting agent
deployer: A fictional regional bank's commercial real estate lending group that runs an underwriting copilot inside Claude Code for its credit analysts.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
incumbent_tools: ARGUS for the occasional mixed-use deal
top_tasks: Size permanent and bridge loans on LTV, DSCR and debt-yield tests and find the binding constraint
Stress NOI, rate and value for the credit memo and show the refinance gap on maturing loans
Tie out the amortization schedule and balloon in the term sheet
hardest_task: A 312-unit garden-style loan in Plano comes up for refinance: T-12 NOI of about $3.18M, sponsor value $52M, existing balance $34.5M, and the bank's policy is 70% LTV, 1.25x DSCR and 8% debt yield at roughly 6.25% on a 30-year amortization. The credit memo needs a one-page stress grid (NOI down 5% and 10%, rate up 100 bp, value moving with NOI) and the refinance gap in each cell, and the committee will check every figure against the analyst's Excel model.
data_it_needs: Sized-loan math with a clear binding constraint, stress grids, schedule tie-outs, and ideally CMBS and sales comps and owner of record for Dallas and Tarrant parcels (registry).
dealbreakers: A number that differs from Excel without a disclosed convention; silent acceptance of unit mistakes; no way to cite the source for a market fact.
budget_note: Would expense up to a low three-figure monthly tool fee per analyst seat without procurement; anything touching borrower data needs a vendor review, and tool calls here send loan terms to a third party.

deployer: A fictional institutional real estate investment manager's valuation group that runs a Python agent to prepare quarterly marks and appraisal-review checks for a grocery-anchored retail portfolio.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
top_tasks: Run property DCFs from the rent roll and reconcile to the direct-cap value for quarterly marks
Check third-party appraisals: recompute the cap rate, reserves and below-the-line adjustments
Report portfolio WALT and rollover exposure by rent
hardest_task: For a 52,500 SF grocery-anchored center ($11.5M basis, 42,000 SF anchor with 15 years left and 10% bumps every five years, two shop leases rolling in years 3 and 10), build a 7-year DCF with probabilistic rollover, TI/LC and a 6.75% exit cap on forward NOI, reconcile it to a direct-cap value within about 2%, and make the numbers tie to the ARGUS run the committee already saw.
data_it_needs: A DCF that exposes its conventions and lets me express stepped anchor rents; direct-cap with reserves and adjustments; cap-rate and sales evidence by market with citations; GSA-style lease comps are not relevant to grocery.
dealbreakers: Undisclosed conventions that move value by more than rounding; no way to express step rents; unverifiable market evidence.
budget_note: An institutional team pays for data, not for arithmetic it can write in Excel; a tool fee under a few hundred dollars a month is irrelevant, but vendor review of anything that receives rent rolls is not.

deployer: A fictional Phoenix hotel owner-operator's asset management office that keeps a private Custom GPT for its owner and two asset managers to review monthly operating statements for four full-service and resort hotels.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Turn each hotel's monthly P&L into occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, TRevPAR, GOP and NOI for the owner report
Spot unit and period mistakes in operator statements before they reach the owner
Compare months against budget and prior year
hardest_task: The March statement for a 210-key Scottsdale resort (62 room-nights out of order for a room renovation, 5,674 rooms sold, $1.64M room revenue, $1.12M F&B, $310K other, $1.15M departmental and $850K undistributed expenses, 3% management fee, $210K property tax and insurance, 4% FF&E reserve) has to become a USALI-style ladder for the owner call, and I need the tool to catch operator errors such as annual revenue pasted against a monthly night count.
data_it_needs: USALI-style KPIs and profit ladder; sanity checks on inputs; ideally a comp-set RevPAR index (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: A tool that quietly accepts nonsense (a 90% GOP margin) and returns a clean-looking answer; Actions that fail to import in the GPT builder.
budget_note: Would pay a small monthly amount if the GPT saves an asset manager a few hours of monthly reporting; the owner will not approve more than a software line item of about a hundred dollars.

deployer: A fictional mid-size industrial investment firm whose acquisitions team builds an underwriting agent in Microsoft Copilot Studio, with a Gemini-based second agent for the research group.
connects_via: Microsoft Copilot Studio or Gemini via the published connector docs
top_tasks: Underwrite in-place and speculative leasing on 100k-500k SF logistics buildings and rank competing tenant proposals
Net effective rent and landlord-perspective comparisons for lease-up of a vacant bay
Sanity-check a seller's rent roll: WALT, rollover, mark-to-market
hardest_task: A 120,000 SF bulk-distribution bay in a secondary Midwest market has two proposals: 5 years at $7.25 NNN with 3% bumps, 3 months free, $4 TI and $182K commissions, versus 7 years at $6.95 with 3.5% bumps, 5 months free, $6 TI and $290K commissions, with 3 months of downtime in front of either. The investment committee wants them on one discounted net effective basis from the landlord's side, with the term mismatch called out.
data_it_needs: Landlord-perspective proposal ranking, net effective rent, WALT and rollover math; submarket rent and vacancy comps (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: A connector I cannot register from Copilot Studio or Gemini, or tool schemas the platform rejects; math that differs from the IC model.
budget_note: The acquisitions team has an AI tooling budget but wants a single vendor review; a $49 to $599 monthly line is fine if the connector actually works in Copilot Studio.

deployer: A fictional institutional appraisal and advisory team that keeps a Custom GPT for staff appraisers who value purpose-built student housing near Texas universities and prepare tax-protest support.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
top_tasks: Analyse a by-the-bed rent roll: GPR, loss to lease, concessions, physical and economic occupancy, July/August expiration cliff
Value on direct cap with reserves and below-the-line items
Calendar Texas property tax protest deadlines for each Austin and San Antonio asset
hardest_task: A 240-unit, 960-bed community near UT Austin has leases that nearly all end July 31, individual beds rented at $949 to $1,039 a month, concessions of $500 or two weeks free, and a few preleased beds for next fall. The appraiser needs GPR, loss to lease, concessions and effective rent per bed and per SF from a bed-level rent roll as of November, plus the Travis protest deadline for the next notice.
data_it_needs: Bed-level rent roll math with unit-type summary and expiration schedule; Texas protest deadline with statute citations; ideally comparable sales and cap rates for student housing, which FactLot does not claim to have.
dealbreakers: A rent roll tool that cannot represent beds or preleases; unflagged unit errors; a rules pack that claims verification it does not have.
budget_note: A staff-level tool: if it saves an appraiser an hour per assignment it is worth a small monthly fee, but the firm will not pay for arithmetic it can do in Excel.

role: Small owner-operator, private investor and 1031 agent
deployer: A fictional two-person family company in South Florida that owns a handful of self-storage facilities and uses Claude (a Claude.ai custom connector) as its research and paperwork assistant.
connects_via: Remote MCP from a Claude client (Claude Desktop / Claude.ai connector)
top_tasks: Check 1031 deadlines, identification rules and boot before talking to the QI and CPA
Compare a sale price and debt payoff with candidate replacement assets
Keep a simple cap-rate and loan-sizing check for each acquisition
hardest_task: The family is selling a 78,000 SF Miami-Dade facility for $6.2M with a $2.1M loan payoff, $186K of selling costs and a $1.4M basis, closing December 10. They want to buy an Orlando facility at $5.4M with $1.8M of new debt, identify two backups, and understand what boot they will create and when the clock runs out before they talk to the QI.
data_it_needs: Correct 45- and 180-day dates, identification-rule results, and boot arithmetic they can bring to the QI; ideally listings and comps for storage (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: Wrong dates or a confident tax conclusion; a tool that needs developer setup; anything that looks like tax advice.
budget_note: A small family owner pays a few tens of dollars a month for something that saves a CPA hour, but will not subscribe for an agent that only the free tier is needed for.

deployer: A fictional three-person lease administration firm in northern New Jersey that abstracts leases for small office landlords and keeps a Custom GPT for its abstractors to extract terms and prepare estoppel reviews.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
incumbent_tools: MRI or Yardi lease modules at client sites
a shared drive of scanned leases
top_tasks: Abstract a lease and its amendments into a current-state abstract with the controlling clause for each term
Compare tenant estoppels and rent rolls with the lease and list the differences
Build a critical-dates list (expirations, renewal notices, rent steps)
hardest_task: A 6,420 RSF medical office suite has a 2021 lease and a 2026 First Amendment that extends the term and resets rent. The abstractor must produce the current expiration and rent with page and clause cites, and then test the tenant's estoppel (which states a 2030 expiration) against it, without the GPT inventing a term it never read.
data_it_needs: Quote-on-page verification, amendment precedence, estoppel comparison with citations; a way to see which terms still need a human.
dealbreakers: A tool that marks something verified when the quote does not support it; losing the amendment's controlling effect; leases sent to a third party without terms I can show a client.
budget_note: A three-person shop will pay for a tool that makes abstracts defensible, a modest monthly fee at most; client confidentiality terms matter more than price.

deployer: A fictional two-appraiser Salt Lake City shop that values single-tenant net lease properties for community banks and keeps a Custom GPT that does the first-pass income work.
connects_via: ChatGPT Custom GPT importing the OpenAPI 3.0 spec as Actions
incumbent_tools: county recorder lookups done by hand
top_tasks: Build the rent schedule for a net lease with stepped rent and show total and per-year rent
Direct-capitalize in-place rent and show the implied cap rate on a price
Run a hold-period IRR and NPV with a renewal-based reversion for the bank's file
hardest_task: A 9,100 SF single-tenant pharmacy on a 12-year remaining NNN lease at $22.50/SF, 10% bumps every five years, is offered at $3.15M. I need the stepped rent schedule, the implied cap rate (6.5% on in-place NOI), and an IRR and NPV over the 12 years that assumes a renewal bump and a 7.25% reversion cap with 1.5% sale costs, all reproducible for the bank's review appraiser.
data_it_needs: Stepped rent schedules, direct cap with implied cap rate, IRR and NPV; net lease sales comps for Utah (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: A calculator I cannot reproduce in Excel; step rents I cannot enter; slow or unreliable Actions in the GPT.
budget_note: A small shop pays for time saved on the first pass; free is fine for arithmetic, and a hosted key at about fifty dollars a month would need to save several hours.

deployer: A fictional mid-size digital-infrastructure investment firm whose acquisitions team uses Claude Code with plugins to underwrite powered-shell and wholesale data center deals.
connects_via: Claude Code with the FactLot plugin
incumbent_tools: CBRE and JLL data center market reports
a legal review checklist for hyperscale MSAs
top_tasks: Rank competing wholesale tenant proposals per kW on one discounted basis
Net effective rent per kW or MW after free rent, TI and commissions
Size debt on stabilized cash flow with DSCR and debt-yield tests
hardest_task: A 4 MW (4,000 kW) wholesale hall in a secondary market has two proposals: a 15-year hyperscaler deal at $145 per kW per month ($1,740 a year) with 3% bumps, 2 months free, $300/kW of TI and $900K commissions, and a 10-year enterprise deal at $155/kW/month ($1,860 a year) with 3.5% bumps, $150/kW TI and $520K commissions. The IC wants them ranked per kW on a landlord discounted net effective basis at 8.5% with the term difference called out, and power pass-through kept separate.
data_it_needs: Per-kW and per-MW lease economics with the unit handled correctly, term mismatch flagged; power cost treatment stated; ideally market rate comps per kW (not in FactLot).
dealbreakers: Per-SF-only tools; a unit mistake that silently shifts a rent by 12x; claims of data center support that fall apart on the first call.
budget_note: Underwriting tool budgets are tiny compared with deal size; a $49 key is nothing if it saves a day, but only if the per-kW outputs are right the first time.

deployer: A fictional two-person New York City fee-appraisal practice that values small mixed-use buildings for lenders and keeps a Python script that calls tool APIs for first-pass income work.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
incumbent_tools: ACRIS and PLUTO lookups by hand
top_tasks: Roll up an apartment rent roll (GPR, loss to lease, concessions, vacancy) and annualize
Value the ground-floor retail by DCF from its leases and combine with residential NOI for a direct-cap conclusion
Pull recorded sales, owner and Local Law 97 exposure for the property (not available hosted)
hardest_task: A six-story, 9,300 SF mixed-use walk-up in Brooklyn: twelve one-bedroom apartments (about $4,100-$4,900 a month; one vacant; two leases with a month free) over two ground-floor retail leases (1,800 SF cafe at $95 and 1,500 SF salon at $110 NNN). The appraiser needs a residential effective rent roll, a retail DCF at a 6.25% exit cap, and a combined direct-cap value near 5.25%, plus ACRIS sales and the building's Local Law 97 position for the lender file.
data_it_needs: Rent roll and DCF arithmetic that I can recompute; NYC recorded sales, ownership and LL97 emissions limits with citations (the materials say these exist in the pipeline but are not open hosted).
dealbreakers: Math that does not reproduce in Excel; claims of NYC data coverage that I cannot query; a rules pack that is only a draft and presented as authoritative.
budget_note: A two-person shop pays for NYC data (sales, ownership, LL97), not for arithmetic; it would consider a monthly fee if NYC lookups were open.

role: Due diligence and legal review agent
deployer: A fictional institutional manufactured-housing investor's acquisitions legal and diligence group that runs a TypeScript agent to check seller representations against documents before closing.
connects_via: REST calls from the deployer's own Python or TypeScript agent code
incumbent_tools: a virtual data room with Q&A logs
T-12 normalization spreadsheets prepared by an analyst
top_tasks: Check a seller's T-12 for footing errors and normalise it onto a standard chart of accounts with every line cited
Verify seller and OM statements about lot lease terms (rent increase caps, notice periods) against the lease form
Package verified facts so counsel and lenders can check them and detect tampering
hardest_task: A 410-pad manufactured housing community's OM says lot-rent increases are capped at 3% a year and shows $798K of NOI. The agent must tie each statement to the lot lease form and the T-12 with page-and-quote citations, find where the numbers do not foot, and hand counsel a package that the lender's agent can check independently.
data_it_needs: Quote-on-page verification, T-12 spreading with footing checks, claim checking, tamper-evident packages; a manufactured-housing chart of accounts (pads, homes, utility reimbursements) would help.
dealbreakers: A verifier that says 'supported' for a quote that is about a different term and presents it as legal assurance; document text sent to a third party without clear no-storage terms.
budget_note: Diligence budgets are per deal; a monthly key at the Team level would be unremarkable if the no-storage, no-model claims were contractually backed, which the customer-documents page says is a policy, not yet a contract.
